note: Research registry. The list of sources behind the model is config, not code; new studies are added here with a version. The v2 exposure blend and its weights are validated in analysis/calibrate.py (see CALIBRATION.md); nothing here is set by a language model.

sources.name: O*NET 29.1
sources.use: Occupation task lists, work activities, work context, job zones; SOC mapping.

sources.name: Eloundou et al. (2023), GPTs are GPTs
sources.use: LLM task exposure for the AI/software axis (measure beta).

sources.name: O*NET Work Context
sources.use: Physical/manual variables for the robotics proxy; the routine/structured-work risk factor.

sources.name: O*NET Work Activities
sources.use: The interpersonal-work factor, the strongest backtest-validated protector.

sources.name: Frey & Osborne (2017)
sources.use: Engineering-bottleneck theory: routine, structured work is the automatable part. Sets the research prior on the robotics/routine direction.

sources.name: BLS OEWS
sources.use: Employment and wages by occupation and metro; the employment-change outcome the model is calibrated against.

sources.name: BLS Employment Projections
sources.use: SOC-keyed projected employment change (occupation demand outlook).

sources.name: Felten, Raj & Seamans AIOE
sources.use: Independent AI Occupational Exposure index; used only for convergent validity (not fit on). Our AI sub-score correlates ~0.86 with it.

sources.name: Webb (2020), patent-based exposure
sources.use: Would add a patent-based robot/AI exposure measure; no cleanly public per-occupation file (author data is email-gated), so documented as a gap, not used.

sources.name: BLS CPI-U
sources.use: Inflation adjustment for the wage-trajectory signal.
